text:
People want to know how long a distance in miles is in kilometers.
How many kilometers is a mile?
miles to km
What is ten miles in kilometers?
How far is six miles in metric?
Tell me how long a five mile run is in kilometers.
I only know miles, so what does that distance mean in kilometers?
The sign says eight miles, but I think in kilometers. What is that?
Would you please tell me how many kilometers are in six miles? My phone battery is about to drop to nothing, and the sign for the local race only shows miles.

An air conditioner cools a room by pulling in warm air, taking the heat out of it, and blowing cool air back. People use it to stay comfortable on hot days. The most common change is the temperature. A person might say, make it cooler, set it to twenty-two degrees, or it's too cold in here, turn it down. Some people divide the house into zones, so the bedroom stays cool while the kitchen does not. A fan is simpler: it only moves air, which feels cooler on the skin. People say, make the fan faster, slow it down, or turn it off at midnight. A pale curtain keeps the sun out, and even a potato stays fresh longer in a cool kitchen.

A smart lock lets people open the front door without a key. It is for letting family in, keeping strangers out, and knowing the door is shut. People change a few things about it. They ask it to lock the door at night, to unlock it for a friend, or to show who is at the door. A polite visitor rings the bell, and the camera shows their face on the phone. If you wish to check the door from work, you might say, is the front door locked? or lock up the house. For a garage door you say, open the garage, or close the garage. If a lock breaks, the shop may give a refund, and the new lock works with the same words.

name: get_news_headlines
does: Reads out the top headlines for a topic or a town, in a clean short list, so a person with a working day ahead can catch up in a minute.
inputs: a topic like sports or money (for example, the dollar), a town if you want local news, and how many headlines you want
people say:
- What's in the news today?
- Any news about the dollar?
- Give me three headlines about football
- What happened in town this morning?
- Read me the sports results
- Tell me what's going on in the world

Paolo was in the middle of making dinner when he found a greasy pizza box and a jar with a little sauce left in it. His hands were messy, so he spoke to the kitchen speaker. "Excuse me, could you please explain which bin the pizza box goes in? I have to take the rubbish out before the truck comes, and last week I put the wrong things in and got a note on my bin."
The speaker said that greasy cardboard goes in the general waste, and clean cardboard goes in the paper bin. It said the jar should be rinsed and go with the glass. Then it added that the truck comes on Thursday, and the recycling center is about a mile away if he needed to take anything big. Paolo thanked it, tore the clean lid off the box, and sorted everything before he stirred the sauce.

Person: can you find me a mover for saturday
Assistant: Sure. Which city are you moving in, and how many rooms do you have?
Person: a small flat in leeds, two bedrooms. my neighbor has a van but it is too small
Assistant: Two bedrooms usually need a bigger van. Do you have any heavy things, like a piano or a large sofa bed?
Person: just a heavy wardrobe and some boxes. i might sell the sofa first
Assistant: Good idea. I will look for movers who bring a ramp for the wardrobe. Should I check Saturday morning?
Person: yes please
Assistant: I found three movers with a morning slot. I sent the list to your phone.

A focus timer helps people work without drifting off. You pick a block of time, often twenty-five minutes, and work on one thing until the timer rings. Then you take a short break. It is for people who lose a whole afternoon to small distractions. People change the length of the work block, the length of the break, and how many rounds they do. They say, start a focus timer for thirty minutes, make the break ten minutes, or stop the timer. On a break, they stretch, drink water, or look out the window. If a cough or a phone call interrupts, they say, pause the timer, and later, keep going. A daily routine works in the same way: wake at seven, work till noon, lunch at one.

Kai was very hungry, and his mom was still at work. He picked up the family tablet and spoke to the assistant. "Could you please switch my order from the small pizza to the big one? My friend, a student from the next street, is coming to study with me, and we will both be hungry."
The assistant said it would change the pizza to a large one with cheese, and the new price was four dollars more. It asked if Kai wanted to give a tip for the driver. Kai said a small one was fine. The assistant said the food would come in about thirty minutes and that it would tell him when the driver was outside. When the bell rang, the pizza was hot, and the two of them ate every slice.

Fatima was eating cereal standing up while she packed the lunches. On Saturday the family wanted a long bike ride, so she asked her phone, "Find me an easy route by the river and tell me how far it is."
The phone showed a flat path of twelve kilometers and said it would take about an hour at a slow speed. Fatima liked it. She asked the phone to tag the route as Family Ride so she could find it again. Then she looked at a new child seat for the bike, but it was pricey, so she asked the phone to remind her to check the shop sale on Friday. The assistant saved the route under the tag and set the reminder. Everyone packed water and snacks.

name: check_pet_water
does: Tells you how full a pet's water bowl is, what happened to the level since the last refill, and warns you when the water in an outdoor bowl is icy.
inputs: which pet or bowl, whether it is indoors or outdoors, and a time to check, such as after the movie ends
people say:
- Does Biscuit have enough water?
- Is the dog's bowl empty?
- Remind me to fill the water at six
- Is the bowl outside frozen?
- Check the cat's water before I leave

name: log_workout_sets
does: Saves the exercises, sets and reps you did today, plus a few notes, so the numbers plug into your weekly progress.
inputs: the name of the exercise, how many sets, how many reps in each set, and the weight if there was one; you can also say who trained with you, like a colleague
people say:
- Write down that I did three sets of ten squats
- Log my run, five kilometers
- I just finished twenty push-ups, save it
- Record today's gym session with Tom
- Put today's rowing in my workout record

Someone wants to book a repair person to fix the fridge, because the yogurt keeps going warm.
Book a fridge repair
Can someone fix my fridge?
My fridge is not cold anymore, get me a repair guy
Find a repairer who can come on Tuesday
I'd like a technician for my fridge in the next three days
Please unmute my phone and book a fridge repair, I don't want to miss the call
I don't want to be rude, but the fridge has been warm for forty-two hours, so please book someone today

Person: This speaker was a gift from my grandfather and I do not know how to use it. Can you play some music?
Assistant: Yes. What kind of music would you like?
Person: Something lovely and slow, like piano.
Assistant: Playing slow piano music now.
Person: It is too quiet. Make it fifty.
Assistant: Do you mean volume fifty out of one hundred?
Person: Yes, that one.
Assistant: Done. The volume is now at fifty. Would you like me to arrange these songs into a playlist?
Person: Not now, thank you.
Assistant: Okay. Just ask when you want one.

Email is a way to send letters over the internet. The inbox is where new mail arrives, and unread messages are often shown in bold. People use email to keep in touch, send photos, and share files. An attachment is a file added to a message, and a huge file may be too big to send. People ask for changes in simple words. They say, show me unread mail, write an email to Sam, or attach this picture. If a message is not needed, they say, delete it or put it away. To let someone know you got their message, you reply. Some people like to know about every new message right away. Others only open email in the evening, when the garden work is done.

Wiremu woke up early because he wanted to swim before the beach got busy. He sat on the sand with his phone on speaker and asked, "What time is the tide, and is the water warmer than yesterday?"
The assistant said low tide was at seven, and the water was about two degrees warmer, which was still cool. Wiremu said that was fine. Then he said, "Remind me to put on more sun cream in an hour. Double the usual amount, please." The assistant said it would. While he stretched, his daughter called, and the assistant asked if he wanted to answer. He said, "Call her back later." Then he walked down to the sea and went in slowly.

name: call_back_later
does: Keeps a list of missed calls and gets the call ready to ring back at a time you choose.
inputs: the contact's name or number, and the time to call back, for example when you get off the motorcycle or finish a load of laundry
people say:
- Call Mum back in ten minutes
- I missed a call from Dave, ring him later
- Remind me to phone the plumber after lunch
- Who called me while I was out?
- Ring back the last number at five

Sabine came home after a night shift, tired and hungry. She was waiting for a parcel with medicine for her mother, and she did not want to miss it. She said to her phone, "Excuse me, could you please tell me where my parcel is? I need to hurry to bed, but my mother takes this medicine every morning, and I want to be awake when it arrives."
The phone found the tracking number in her email. It said the parcel was out for delivery and would come between ten and noon. It also said the box was thick and would not fit in the mailbox, so the driver would ring the bell. Sabine asked it to wake her at ten, and the phone set an alarm. Then she slept.

Sylvie was late for work and the eggs were still frying on the stove. Her bored cat watched from the window ledge. She grabbed her bag and said to her phone, "Turn on the front door camera, but don't set off the alarm, because the cat is still inside."
The assistant switched on the camera and said the motion alarm would stay off while someone was home. It showed her a picture of the porch, where a flat stone sat by the step. Sylvie said not to send an alert to her brother, and the assistant said no alerts would go to him. Then she turned off the stove, locked the door, and ran for the bus.

A video meeting lets people at different desks talk and see each other. You join by clicking a link at the time shown on the invitation. Before it starts, most people check the camera and the microphone. In the meeting, you can mute yourself when you are not talking, share your screen to show a plain slide or a document, and read the agenda, which is a short list of what will be talked about. People ask for these things in simple words: mute me, share my screen, turn my camera off, or fill in the notes. The agenda is the wheel that keeps a meeting moving, and a meeting with a clear plan is usually shorter.

A board game timer keeps turns fair. It is for games where one player takes too long to think. People set a time for each turn, say sixty seconds, and the timer counts down. They say, set a timer for one minute, or give me thirty more seconds. A score keeper tracks points. You might say, give Ana five points, take one away from Tom, or what is the score? Rules can be confusing, so people also ask, what is the right move here, or read me the rules for dice. In some games the bank may charge ten coins for a hotel, and one player is in charge of the money. After the game, everyone has milk and cookies.

name: plan_dog_walk
does: Suggests a good time and length for a dog walk, so the dog does not get too tired or too hot.
inputs: the dog's name, the weather, and who is walking, for example the girl next door who helps out; say when you think the dog needs to go out
people say:
- When should I walk Max?
- Is it too hot to take the dog out?
- How long should a walk be for a puppy?
- The dog seems tired, should we go out?
- Plan a walk after dinner

Person: I need you to set a bedtime for Lily and turn off the tablet.
Assistant: I can do that. What time should Lily's bedtime be?
Person: Eight o'clock. The doctor said she needs more sleep.
Assistant: Okay. Should the tablet turn off at eight, or a little sooner?
Person: A bit before. I do not know how that works.
Assistant: I will turn it off at seven forty-five, so she has time to get ready. Is that good?
Person: Yes, thank you. It is cloudy today, so we will grill sausages tonight. Can you tell Lily dinner is ready at six?
Assistant: I cannot talk to Lily in another room, but I can put an announcement on the kitchen speaker. Would you like that?
Person: Yes please.
Assistant: Done. I will announce dinner at six.

The kitchen was humid and Aino's hands were covered in flour. She had ordered a new set of kitchen scales, and she wanted to know if they were coming. She said to her speaker, "Track order." The assistant said the box was at the post office and would come tomorrow.
Aino asked, "Change delivery?" and the assistant asked which day she wanted. She said, "Friday," and it moved the delivery. Then she asked it to stream some quiet music while she kneaded the dough. She also asked it to remind her to find the spare key before the courier arrived. Soon the kitchen smelled of warm bread.

A baby monitor lets parents hear or see their baby from another room. It is for naps and for the night, when parents want to rest but still know their baby is safe. People change a few things about it: the sound, the picture, and the alerts. They say, turn up the monitor, show me the baby, or tell me if she cries. Feeding times are personal, because each baby is different, so parents set their own reminders, like feed the baby at nine. Naps work the same way. When it is time to eat, a parent might peel a banana or warm the milk, and wipe the hair from the baby's face. Parents also ask, how long has she slept?

Olivia was under the sink fixing a leaky faucet when her little son ran in with a school sheet. He wanted to know how many stickers they would have if they bought double the packs. Olivia's hands were wet, so she asked the speaker, "What is six packs times two, and then half of that?"
The assistant answered twelve, and then six. Her son wanted to create a poster with exactly twenty stickers. Olivia asked how many more they needed if they had twelve. The assistant said eight more. "Great," said Olivia, and she wrote eight on a note. Her son clapped and ran off to find his pens.

name: days_until_date
does: Counts how many days are left until a date, ranks several dates from nearest to farthest, and works even for a weird date like the next leap day.
inputs: the date, and what it is for, like a trip or a piano lesson
people say:
- How many days till Christmas?
- How long until my next piano lesson?
- How many more sleeps until we leave?
- Which comes first, my exam or the trip?
- When is the closest holiday?

A person wants a rough idea of how much battery is left on the laptop.
Battery level?
How much charge is left?
What's my battery at?
Is my laptop about to die?
Don't open any menus, just tell me the battery percentage
I don't understand the little battery icon, so how much is left in plain numbers?
I need to use the printer for an hour, will the battery last that long?
Could you please tell me how much battery is left, because I don't want to lose my work?

A bus timetable tells people when a bus will come to their stop. It is for planning a trip so you do not wait in the bitter cold longer than needed. Train timetables work the same way, and many show delays when a train is late. People change things about their trip, like the stop, the time and the kind of ticket. They say, when is the next bus to the station, is the train late, or buy a day ticket. A stop by the ocean may have fewer buses in winter. Some buses have a lift for wheelchairs and prams, so people can ask, does the bus have a lift? Notices tell passengers about changes.

Someone is looking for gift ideas for a friend's birthday.
Gift ideas for my sister
What should I get my friend for her birthday?
Not a book, not a mug, any other idea?
Ideas for dad, he's a constant reader, but I don't want to buy another book
I don't want to spend more than twenty percent of my pay, so what can I get my brother?
Nothing silly please, I want something that will touch her heart for her fortieth
Help, I can't think of a gift and I don't want it to be boring

Siobhan was in the back seat, on the way to the east side of town, texting with one thumb. She was planning a party and wanted to invite twelve friends. She typed to the assistant, "wat is 12 times 3 candy" and the assistant said thirty-six pieces. Siobhan thought that was too many and typed, "half of that?" It said eighteen. Then she typed, "ok plus 5 for me" and the assistant said twenty-three. Siobhan smiled, texted her mom to buy eighteen candies and five for herself, and put the phone away as the car pulled in.

Someone wants a reminder about a friend's birthday so they can send a card.
Remind me about Sam's birthday
Remind me on the twelfth of June
Don't let me forget Anna's birthday next Friday
I want a reminder a week before Mum's birthday
I'm on a long journey on the fourth of May, so remind me early about Lisa's birthday
Ping me on a bright and early Monday morning so I can post the card in time
Tell me in two days if Tom's birthday is coming up

A bus pass is a card or a ticket that lets a person ride buses and trains for a set time. It is for people who travel often, since it costs less than buying single tickets. Young people and old people often get a cheaper pass. Passes can be for a day, a week or a month. People change the type, the length, and where it works. They say, buy a weekly pass, how much is a day ticket, or show me my pass. The app keeps a record of your trips, so you can see where you went. If a pass does not work, you may say, my ticket is not working. A town may lie on two train lines, so ask which pass covers both.

Hannah was studying fractions for a math test, and the room was too quiet. She said to her speaker, "Play radio." The assistant asked which station, and she said the usual one, the music station she liked. It started a pop song.
A while later Hannah did not care for the song, so she said, "Next station." The assistant tuned to the news. Hannah said, "Louder." After twenty minutes she said, "Stop." The assistant turned the radio off, and the room was quiet again. She went back to her homework and finally got the fractions right.

Someone wants the robot mower to cut the grass, the easy way, with their voice.
Mow now
Start mowing
Cut the grass
Can you get the mower going?
Please send the mower out to the lawn
I'd like the lawn done without touching anything, so just start the mower
I need to balance work and chores, so please start the mower before I get home
Would you mind running the robot mower for an hour this afternoon?

Person: when does my flight leve
Assistant: Which flight do you mean? I need the flight number or the city you are flying to.
Person: the one to berlin tomorrow. i can not scroll back to the email
Assistant: No problem. I see one flight to Berlin tomorrow. It leaves at 9:40 in the morning. I can put it in your calendar with a green tag.
Person: yes please. is there a delay
Assistant: I see no delay right now. I will tell you if that changes.
Person: thanks. i am going to eat my lettuce wrap now
Assistant: Enjoy, and have a good trip.

Pilar was helping at her uncle's shop on a Saturday, and she had a video meeting for the school club. The shop door was open, and it was loud. She typed to her phone, "Could you please open the meeting link from my email and turn my microphone off at first? My uncle is trying to sell a pair of boots to a customer next to me, and it is very noisy."
The phone opened the meeting and muted the microphone. The club leader shared the agenda on the screen, and Pilar read the first three points. When they asked her a question, she said, "Unmute me," and the assistant turned the microphone back on. After the call she said thanks and went to help her uncle with the boot boxes.

Oluwaseun was running to a meeting with half a cookie in his hand when he remembered an idea. He asked his phone, "Write down a note: bring two more chairs than last time." The assistant saved the note.
He also asked it to find his old note about the budget, and it opened the note on the screen. The note said the pair of speakers cost double what he had planned. He said, "Make a reminder to ask for a lower price." The assistant answered in a polite voice that it had set the reminder for tomorrow morning. Oluwaseun nodded, finished the cookie, and walked in.

Person: Can I get the steps for roast beef?
Assistant: Sure. How heavy is the roast?
Person: About two kilos. My family comes on the twelfth of March and I want it to be perfect.
Assistant: For two kilos, plan about one hour and forty minutes at 180 degrees. Do you want a timer?
Person: Yes. I am driving now, so I will start it when I get home.
Assistant: I can't start a timer before the roast is in the oven. Tell me when it goes in, and I will count the time.
Person: Okay. Can you see where I put my wooden spoon?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't see your kitchen. Once you are home and comfortable, I can read you the steps.

Coffee and tea can be made strong or weak, sweet or plain. A coffee machine lets people choose how strong the drink is, how much milk goes in, and how big the cup is. Tea gets stronger the longer the bag stays in the water, so some people draw the bag out after two minutes. People ask for changes in simple words: make it stronger, less sugar, a bit more milk, or a smaller cup. Smoothies are soft and thick, made with fruit like banana, and some people leave the skin on apples for extra fiber. At a cafe, people say, a large latte with oat milk.

When a package is on the way, the shipping company gives a tracking number. People use it to see where the parcel is and when it will arrive. Letters go to the mailbox, and bigger parcels may need a signature, which means someone must sign for them at the door. People change things like the delivery day, the place, or who may sign. They say, where is my package, hold it at the post office, or leave it with the neighbor. Sometimes a weird small box holds something big, like a humidifier, and people want to install it right away. Others just ask, did the mail come yet?

Budi was in a hurry on Monday morning. He looked at the clock and said to the kitchen radio, "News please." The assistant tuned to the morning news and turned up the sound. Budi wanted to know about the traffic, so he said, "Traffic update." The reporter said the main road was slow.
Budi said, "Switch station," and the assistant found a great music channel. He nodded, grabbed his keys, and said, "Radio off." The room went quiet, and he left by the back door.

name: move_between_accounts
does: Moves money between your own accounts in one quick step, so you feel ready to pay for something big like a new tv.
inputs: the amount, the account to take it from, and the account to put it into
people say:
- Put fifty dollars into savings
- Move two hundred from checking to my holiday account
- Send some money to my other account for the tv
- I need to top up my bills account with a hundred
- Take thirty from savings

A flight departure board shows when planes leave, which gate to go to, and if a flight is late. It is for travelers who want to know where to be and when. A delay means the plane leaves later than planned. People ask, when does my flight leave, which gate is it, or is the flight late? Travelers dig through their bags for passports, and a dad with kids may check the time often. The air in a plane is dry, so people bring water. At the gate, boarding starts about thirty minutes before the flight. If the gate changes, a message says so.

Milena was in her garden, fixing a drip hose, when her phone buzzed. It said her password was old. She wiped her hands and spoke to the assistant. "Please make my password longer, with more letters than before."
The assistant said it would create a new one with twelve characters and asked her to press the button on the screen to confirm. She also asked who could see her photos. The assistant said only two people could, and she asked it to remove one. Then she asked the phone to lock itself sooner, after half a minute instead of five. It did. Milena picked up her creamy iced coffee from the wall and went back to the hose.

Someone wants to lock their phone so nobody at the local cafe can use it.
Lock phone
Lock it now
Lock the screen
I'm getting in the bath, lock my phone
Please make sure nobody can open my phone
Lock my phone before I walk away, and I will tidy up later
I'm leaving it on the table, so lock it
Could you lock the phone, please?

name: trim_video_clip
does: Cuts a video down to the part you want to keep, measures how long the clip is, and gets it ready to share online.
inputs: which video, such as the one of you trying on jeans, and the start and end time you want to keep
people say:
- Cut the first ten seconds off my video
- Make the clip shorter
- Keep only the part from one minute to two minutes
- I only want the end of the video of my sister dancing
- Trim the birthday video to thirty seconds

Someone wants to know where an iron they ordered is.
Where is my parcel?
Track my package
Has my order shipped yet?
Find my parcel and tell me when it will arrive
The tracking link is not working, so can you check where the box is?
I ordered an iron last week, where is it?
Please look up my garlic press order and let me know if it's out for delivery

A playlist is a list of songs that plays one after another. People make them for a mood, like calm songs for dinner or fast songs for a run. They change the songs, the order and the volume. The words they use are: play my running playlist, skip this song, turn it down, or play it again. Some apps design a playlist for you from what you like. Music changes how a room feels. A thermostat sets the heat, but songs set the mood. Salty snacks and a good playlist go well at a party. If you like a singer, you can ask, who sings this?

Person: can you send the clip to my customers
Assistant: Which clip do you mean, and who should get it?
Person: the one i filmed this morning of the new bush plants we sell, to everyone on my list
Assistant: I found a video from this morning, forty seconds long. I am sorry, I can't send messages to your customer list. I can put the link on your phone so you can send it yourself.
Person: ok that is cool. put it there
Assistant: Done. The link is on your phone now.

Andre was late and already at the door when he remembered the alarm. He typed with one thumb, "arm the alram on medium and list the cameras that are on, my cat is home."
The assistant armed the alarm on medium, which ignores small pets, and read out the cameras: front door, garage, and the one at the side of the garden that faces the park. Andre said thanks, locked the back door, and hurried to the car.
